    How customer reviews and ratings work

    Customer reviews, including Product Star Ratings, help customers to learn more about the product and decide whether it is the right product for them.

    To calculate the overall star rating and percentage breakdown by star, we do not use a simple average. Instead, our system considers things such as how recent a review is and if the reviewer bought the item on Amazon. It also analyses reviews to verify trustworthiness.

      4 out of 5 stars
      Excellent Colors & Overall Experience Under ₹40K, But Know the Trade-offs
      Reviewed in India on 30 June 2026
      Style Name: Crystal 4K UHD AI 2026 SeriesSize: 55 Inches
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      I spent nearly a month comparing TVs, visiting stores multiple times, watching reviews, and reading long-term owner experiences before making this purchase. Every opinion below is based entirely on my own real-world experience.

      Pros:

      Excellent color reproduction. To my eyes: LG 90/100, Samsung 95/100, Sony 100/100. Sony still has the best picture processing, but Samsung comes surprisingly close for much less money.

      Smooth and responsive Tizen OS.

      Excellent Bluetooth headphone audio quality.

      HDR content looks vibrant and natural.

      Very good browser performance.

      HDMI ARC/eARC works perfectly.

      Cons:

      Motion isn't quite as smooth as LG's implementation. I noticed some ghosting/trailing, especially with subtitles and certain animated content.

      Black bars are more noticeable in a dark room because this is a Direct LED TV.

      No native Kodi or Jellyfin app on Tizen (Plex is available).

      Built-in USB media player doesn't support every subtitle format.

      Smart Hub shows recommendations and promotional content that can't be completely removed.

      I also spent time comparing TCL and Xiaomi TVs. Their Mini LED models definitely offer better black levels and HDR, but I personally found their color tuning too aggressive and oversaturated. They look impressive in a showroom, but for long viewing sessions I preferred Samsung's more natural image. Sony still delivers the best picture overall, but it also costs significantly more.

      Final Verdict: If you can get this TV for around ₹40,000–45,000 (or even less with bank offers and coupons), I think it's an excellent value. I personally wouldn't recommend paying much more than that, because above this price range there are stronger alternatives. If your priorities are natural colors, a smooth interface and reliable day-to-day performance, this TV is easy to recommend. If you need Mini LED blacks, Kodi/Jellyfin support or advanced USB media playback, you should consider an Android TV platform or an external streaming device.

      Samsung TV & Amazon: Extremely Poor Installation and After-Sales Support
      Reviewed in India on 17 October 2026
      Style Name: Crystal 4K UHD AI 2026 SeriesSize: 43 Inches
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      Extremely Disappointing Experience with Both Samsung and Amazon – Poor Product Experience, Installation and Customer Support

      I purchased the Samsung 43-inch Crystal UHD 4K Vision AI 2026 Smart TV (Model: UA43UE86AHULXL) from Amazon, expecting a good product and a hassle-free buying experience. Unfortunately, my experience with BOTH Samsung and Amazon has been extremely disappointing. I regret choosing this combination.

      **1. Amazon's order and installation process was a mess**

      I initially placed the order on 14 October 2026 and carefully checked my home address multiple times. Despite that, the order showed my office address as the shipping address. Amazon Customer Service told me that the address could not be changed, forcing me to cancel the order and purchase the TV again. This wasted my time before I even received the product.

      I placed the order again, and the TV was delivered on 15 October. However, the installation request had not been generated through Amazon. Only the TV delivery and Open Box Inspection service appeared in the order details. I had to spend additional time contacting customer service and figuring out how installation would happen.

      **2. Samsung's installation service was equally disappointing**

      When the Samsung technician arrived on 15 October, he brought installation equipment for a 32-inch TV, even though I had purchased a 43-inch model and had already shared the correct TV model, size and details with him over WhatsApp. I had to wait while he went to arrange the appropriate equipment. Apparently, the customer is expected to wait patiently when the service provider arrives unprepared, but the same consideration is not extended to the customer.

      After installation, I discovered that the rear USB ports were extremely difficult to access because of the adjacent wall/stone structure. I informed the technician shortly after installation. I only needed the TV shifted sideways by approximately 15–20 cm so that I could conveniently connect a USB drive.

      I was not asking for a new installation or a complicated setup. The TV was already mounted and working. Yet I was told that repositioning required paid reinstallation. Samsung Customer Support did not provide a satisfactory solution and directed me towards its service centre, where I was quoted **₹1,100 plus GST** for the work.

      How is a customer supposed to know every practical issue with port accessibility while watching an installation technician mount a TV for the first time? I reported the problem promptly, not weeks later. A customer should not have to become an installation expert to ensure that the USB ports remain accessible.

      **3. Amazon made assurances and then denied them**

      On 16 October, I contacted Amazon again. One representative told me that I could get the work done through a local service provider and that Amazon would reimburse the cost against a proper tax invoice. I specifically discussed getting the work done through Samsung and submitting its invoice.

      During another interaction, a representative told me to forget that arrangement because Amazon would send its own technician within 24 hours. I was given reference number **61950** and relied on that assurance.

      I waited throughout 17 October for the promised technician. When I called again at around 6 PM, I was told that no such commitment was recorded and that Amazon could not help me. One representative had suggested Urban Company, another had promised reimbursement, another had assured me that Amazon would send a technician, and the next representative effectively denied the previous assurances.

      **What is the point of customer service if commitments made by its representatives cannot be trusted?** If Amazon could not arrange the service or reimburse me, it should have said so clearly from the beginning. Instead, I wasted another day waiting for a technician who never arrived.

      The delivery itself was on time, and I am not blaming the delivery personnel. My complaint is specifically about Amazon's order processing, failure to generate the installation request, contradictory customer service responses and lack of accountability after purchase.

      **4. The Smart TV experience itself is disappointing**

      The advertising experience has also been frustrating. Samsung's smart TV interface displays promotional content, and watching YouTube involves frequent advertisements that interrupt viewing. YouTube controls its own ad delivery, but the overall experience on the television has been much more advertising-heavy than I expected.

      I bought a TV to watch movies, shows and videos comfortably, not to feel that I am spending an unreasonable amount of time watching advertisements. Buyers who are sensitive to advertising should research the Smart TV experience carefully before buying.

      **My overall experience has been extremely poor.**

      Samsung has made the installation and service experience unnecessarily difficult, while Amazon's representatives have given contradictory assurances and failed to honour the expectations they created. I have spent hours contacting both companies, repeating the same story, waiting for promised assistance and trying to resolve a relatively minor 15–20 cm repositioning issue.

      The problem is not simply the additional charge. It is the lack of accountability, coordination and respect for the customer's time. Samsung directed me to the service centre, while Amazon ultimately denied responsibility despite its representatives having offered possible solutions.

      I expected far better from two major brands. Based on my personal experience, I would **strongly advise buyers to carefully consider both Samsung's after-sales service and Amazon's installation support before purchasing expensive electronics.** A product should not become this stressful to use immediately after purchase.

      **My TV was delivered on time, but the overall buying, installation and after-sales experience was unacceptable. I would not willingly repeat this experience with either company.**
